content: WikiDoc provides a reference manager that allows users to insert references directly into their text using PubMed ID numbers. Additionally, clicking on the reference takes the user directly to the cited article. This process eliminates the need to manually type references at the end of the article. To insert references, you typically use a number in the text, such as (1) or 1, which corresponds to a reference listed at the end of the document. However, WikiDoc’s automated reference manager simplifies this process. Instead of manually typing references at the end, you insert a code for the reference immediately after the relevant text. This code is generated using a software program, which is described in detail below. The goal of WikiDoc’s reference manager is to create clickable reference lists that link directly to the primary article, making it easier to locate sources. The reference manager supports various identifiers, including PubMed ID (PMID), DrugBank ID, HGNC ID, ISBN, PubMed Central ID, PubChem ID, and URLs. The preferred method for inserting references involves the following steps: 1. Use PubMed to locate the desired article. The PubMed ID (PMID) is typically found at the bottom of the article’s abstract. You can use the search function in your browser to locate the term “PMID,” followed by the unique number (e.g., PMID: 19032997). 2. Copy the PMID and paste it into a software program designed to generate Wiki language code for references. Examples of such software include: SUMSearch Biomedical Citation Maker (converts PMID into Wiki reference markup with embedded SUMSearch links) DOI Wikipedia Reference Generator (converts DOI into Wiki reference markup) DTU Informatics PMID to Cite Journal (converts PMID into Wiki reference markup) OttoBib (converts ISBN into Wiki reference markup) Dave’s Template Filler (converts various identifiers, such as DrugBank ID, HGNC ID, ISBN, PubMed ID, PubMed Central ID, PubChem ID, or URLs, into Wiki reference markup). 3. 4. Submit the information to generate the Wiki language code. 5. Copy the generated Wiki language code. For example, the output for PMID 19032997 might look like this: ``` {{cite journal |author=Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, ''et al '' |title=Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006 |journal=Am Heart J |volume=156 |issue=6 |pages=1035–44 |year=2008 |month=December |pmid=19032997 |doi=10 1016/j ahj 2008 07 029 |url=}} ``` 6. Paste this code directly into the text where you want the superscript reference number to appear. For example: ``` Gibson et al recently summarized the improvements made in clinical outcomes as a result of 15 years of quality improvement efforts in the NRMI registry {{cite journal |author=Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, ''et al '' |title=Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006 |journal=Am Heart J |volume=156 |issue=6 |pages=1035–44 |year=2008 |month=December |pmid=19032997 |doi=10 1016/j ahj 2008 07 029 |url=}} ``` This will generate a clickable reference in the final text. If you prefer not to use the reference manager, you can manually type references. To do this: 1. Place `<ref>` immediately after the sentence where you want the footnote number to appear. 2. Type the reference text between the `<ref>` tags. For example: ``` <ref>Author Name, Title of the Article, Journal Name, Year, Volume, Page Numbers</ref> ``` This will appear as a footnote in the text. If you plan to use the same reference multiple times, assign a name to the reference using the format `<ref name=reference_name>`. To display references at the bottom of the article, use the following code: ``` <references /> ``` This will generate a list of references in small font, organized in two columns, with clickable links to the original articles and abstracts.
